FROM registry.redhat.io/rhel10/rhel-bootc:10.2

# === Custom Repositories (2) ===
COPY config/etc/yum.repos.d/ /etc/yum.repos.d/

# === GPG Keys (1) ===
COPY config/etc/pki/rpm-gpg/ /etc/pki/rpm-gpg/
# Not copied: /etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-redhat-release: the base image ships it (redhat-release, unmodified on the source host)

# "Container Management" degraded (member excluded): members rendered individually

# === Packages (45) ===
RUN dnf install -y \
    aide \
    at \
    autoconf \
    automake \
    bat \
    cmake \
    cockpit \
    cups \
    fd-find \
    fzf \
    gcc \
    gdb \
    git \
    grub2-efi-aa64-cdboot \
    grub2-tools-extra \
    htop \
    httpd \
    info \
    kernel-devel \
    langpacks-en \
    libtool \
    libvirt-daemon-driver-network \
    libvirt-daemon-lock \
    libvirt-daemon-log \
    make \
    man-pages \
    nginx \
    nmap-ncat \
    nodejs \
    python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock \
    python3-pip \
    ripgrep \
    rsync \
    ruby \
    sssd \
    strace \
    tcpdump \
    tmux \
    tree \
    tuned \
    unzip \
    valgrind \
    vim-enhanced \
    wget \
    wireguard-tools \
    && dnf clean all \
    && rm -rf \
        /var/cache/dnf \
        /var/lib/dnf/history* \
        /var/log/dnf* \
        /var/log/hawkey.log \
        /var/log/rhsm

# Not carried: not user-installed on the source host, and nothing this image installs needs it (27)
#   cronie (crond.service was enabled)
#   firewalld (firewalld.service was enabled)
#   rsyslog (rsyslog.service was enabled)
#   sssd-kcm (sssd-kcm.socket was enabled)
#   buildah
#   cronie-anacron
#   crontabs
#   dnf-plugins-core
#   dracut-config-rescue
#   firewalld-filesystem
#   grubby
#   initscripts-rename-device
#   ipset
#   ipset-libs
#   libcap-ng-python3
#   libestr
#   libfastjson
#   libsysfs
#   lshw
#   lsscsi
#   parted
#   prefixdevname
#   python3-firewall
#   python3-nftables
#   rootfiles
#   samba-core-libs
#   samba-ndr-libs

# === Version Locks ===
RUN dnf install -y python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock && \
    dnf versionlock add curl-0:8.12.1-6.el10.* && \
    dnf versionlock add curl-0:8.12.1-6.el10.* && \
    dnf clean all

# === Service Drop-ins ===
# 4 unit drop-in(s): override snippets for systemd units
COPY drop-ins/etc/systemd/system/ /etc/systemd/system/

# === Scheduled Tasks ===
COPY config/etc/systemd/system/ /etc/systemd/system/
# Local timers carried with their configuration or drop-in row (2): driftify-backup.timer, myapp-report.timer
# Converted from cron: 5 timer(s): cron-backup-daily, cron-complex-job, cron-crontab, cron-daily-cleanup-sh, cron-appuser
RUN systemctl enable -- \
    cron-appuser.timer \
    cron-backup-daily.timer \
    cron-complex-job.timer \
    cron-crontab.timer \
    cron-daily-cleanup-sh.timer
# FIXME: 2 at job(s) found — convert to systemd timers or cron
#   at job: 
#   at job: ${SHELL:-/bin/sh} << ''marcinDELIMITER3e00e976''; touch /tmp/driftify-at-probe; marcinDELIMITER3e00e976

# === Configuration Files ===
# 88 config file(s) captured

COPY config/etc/ /etc/

# === Systemd Unit State ===
# FIXME: tmp.mount is masked on the source host, where /tmp is then a directory on the root filesystem. Not carried: the bootc base image mounts /tmp from this unit, and without it /tmp is read-only.
# Omitted: wg-quick@wg0.service (its configuration /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf holds a redacted value; provision the secret on the deployed host and enable the unit there)
RUN systemctl set-default -- graphical.target
RUN systemctl enable -- \
    driftify-also-member.service \
    getty@tty2.service \
    httpd.service \
    nginx.service \
    myapp-report.timer
RUN systemctl disable -- \
    cockpit.socket \
    cups.socket \
    iscsid.socket \
    virtnetworkd-admin.socket \
    virtnetworkd-ro.socket \
    virtnetworkd.socket
RUN systemctl mask -- \
    bluetooth.service \
    kdump.service
# Advisory: cups.service is enabled on the source host. Not carried: systemctl enable on it also enables cups.socket (named by Also=), which is not enabled there.
#   To reproduce the source host, add after the configuration COPY:
#     RUN systemctl enable -- cups.service
#     RUN systemctl disable -- cups.socket
#   Each command follows Also= in its turn. Check the result with systemctl is-enabled.
# Advisory: driftify-also-main.service is enabled on the source host. Not carried: /etc/systemd/system/driftify-also-main.service sets [Install] for driftify-also-main.service, so the units systemctl enable reaches through Also= in the image may not be the ones recorded.
#   After reading that file, add after the configuration COPY:
#     RUN systemctl enable -- driftify-also-main.service
# Advisory: iscsid.service is enabled on the source host. Not carried: systemctl enable on it also enables iscsid.socket (named by Also=), which is not enabled there.
#   To reproduce the source host, add after the configuration COPY:
#     RUN systemctl enable -- iscsid.service
#     RUN systemctl disable -- iscsid.socket
#   Each command follows Also= in its turn. Check the result with systemctl is-enabled.
# Advisory: virtnetworkd.service is enabled on the source host. Not carried: systemctl enable on it also enables virtnetworkd.socket, virtnetworkd-ro.socket and virtnetworkd-admin.socket (named by Also=), which are not enabled there.
#   To reproduce the source host, add after the configuration COPY:
#     RUN systemctl enable -- virtnetworkd.service
#     RUN systemctl disable -- virtnetworkd.socket
#     RUN systemctl disable -- virtnetworkd-ro.socket
#     RUN systemctl disable -- virtnetworkd-admin.socket
#   Each command follows Also= in its turn. Check the result with systemctl is-enabled.
# Advisory: multi-user.target.wants/driftify-static.service is a link on the source host that driftify-static.service's [Install] section there does not make (it names no link: none, only Also=, or a list a drop-in reset to empty). Not carried.
#   To carry it, add after the configuration COPY: RUN systemctl add-wants -- multi-user.target driftify-static.service
# Advisory: multi-user.target.upholds/driftify-upheld.service is not carried: the unit's [Install] section cannot be relied on (enabling the unit would also make an .upholds link).
#   An .upholds link starts driftify-upheld.service while multi-user.target is active and restarts it whenever it stops, so adding it for a unit that becomes inactive after it exits, such as a oneshot service without RemainAfterExit=yes, produces a restart loop. A RHEL 9 target does not honor it. To add it, put Upholds=driftify-upheld.service in a drop-in for multi-user.target.
# Advisory: driftify-upheld.service is not carried: its [Install] section on the source host cannot be relied on (enabling the unit would also make an .upholds link), and these files under /etc/systemd/system change it: /etc/systemd/system/driftify-upheld.service.
#   The image's links for driftify-upheld.service can differ from the source host's, including links its package install made before these files are copied. Check them with systemctl is-enabled in the image.

# === Language Packages ===
# WARNING: python3 not found in RPM package list — add it before this section

# WARNING: This environment contains packages with C extensions that may need
# native compilation toolchains (gcc, python3-devel).
# pip packages: /opt/myapp/venv (from requirements.txt, RPM-filtered)
COPY language-packages/pip/77fce1b75e7a/requirements.txt '/tmp/venv-requirements.txt'
RUN python3 -m venv '/opt/myapp/venv' \
    && '/opt/myapp/venv'/bin/pip install -r '/tmp/venv-requirements.txt' \
    && rm '/tmp/venv-requirements.txt'

# pip packages: /opt/legacy-app/venv (from requirements.txt, RPM-filtered)
COPY language-packages/pip/3ee13faaf2c5/requirements.txt '/tmp/venv-requirements.txt'
RUN python3 -m venv --system-site-packages '/opt/legacy-app/venv' \
    && '/opt/legacy-app/venv'/bin/pip install -r '/tmp/venv-requirements.txt' \
    && rm '/tmp/venv-requirements.txt'

# WARNING: This environment contains packages with C extensions that may need
# native compilation toolchains (gcc, python3-devel).
# pip packages: /opt/shared-venv (detected via dist-info — transitive deps may differ)
# Uncomment after verifying package list is complete:
# RUN python3 -m venv --system-site-packages '/opt/shared-venv' \
#     && '/opt/shared-venv'/bin/pip install black==26.10.1 click==8.5.1 iniconfig==2.3.1 mypy_extensions==1.2.0 pathspec==1.1.1 pip==23.3.2 platformdirs==4.14.5 pluggy==1.7.0 Pygments==2.21.0 pytest==9.2.0 pytokens==0.4.1

# pip packages: /var/www/django-app/venv (detected via dist-info — transitive deps may differ)
# Uncomment after verifying package list is complete:
# RUN python3 -m venv '/var/www/django-app/venv' \
#     && '/var/www/django-app/venv'/bin/pip install asgiref==3.13.0 Django==4.2 pip==23.3.2 sqlparse==0.6.1

# npm packages: /opt/webapp (from package-lock.json)
COPY language-packages/npm/23f9725da273/package.json '/opt/webapp'/package.json
COPY language-packages/npm/23f9725da273/package-lock.json '/opt/webapp'/package-lock.json
RUN cd '/opt/webapp' && npm ci --production

# npm packages: /var/www/webapp (from package-lock.json)
COPY language-packages/npm/77d99b8f1c52/package.json '/var/www/webapp'/package.json
COPY language-packages/npm/77d99b8f1c52/package-lock.json '/var/www/webapp'/package-lock.json
RUN cd '/var/www/webapp' && npm ci --production

# npm global packages: /usr/local/lib/node_modules (detected via npm list -g)
RUN npm install -g -- '@angular/cli' '@types/node' 'pm2' 'typescript'

# gem packages: /usr/local/share/gems (low confidence — review required)

# === Container Workloads (4) ===
COPY quadlet/ /etc/containers/systemd/

# === Compose Stacks (reference only) ===
# === Compose stacks detected ===
# The following compose stacks were running on the source host.
# These are application workloads, not OS configuration.
# See compose/ in the build context for the original files.
#
# Consider converting to Quadlet units — .container files under
# /etc/containers/systemd/ that let systemd manage your container
# workloads natively.
#   man quadlet(5)
#   https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.html
#   https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/html/building_running_and_managing_containers/porting-containers-to-systemd-using-podman
#
#   - /opt/myapp/docker-compose.yml (2 services)

# === Kernel and Boot Configuration ===
# Tuned profile: throughput-performance
RUN echo "throughput-performance" > /etc/tuned/active_profile
RUN echo "manual" > /etc/tuned/profile_mode

# === Security & Access Control ===
# SELinux file contexts (1 custom rule). Labels for image content are computed
# when bootc pulls the image, from the image's own policy under /etc/selinux, so
# a rule only needs to be in the policy store: no restorecon at build time. Each
# rule below is either a command or a FIXME saying why it could not be one. Data
# you restore into /var (/var/srv included) keeps the labels it arrived with;
# run restorecon -R on it before starting the services that use it.
# The file context and port rules below need semanage, which this base does not
# carry; policycoreutils-python-utils provides it.
RUN dnf install -y policycoreutils-python-utils \
    && dnf clean all \
    && rm -rf \
        /var/cache/dnf \
        /var/lib/dnf/history* \
        /var/log/dnf* \
        /var/log/hawkey.log \
        /var/log/rhsm
# Each rule removes its own key from the local store if present, then adds it, or
# modifies it when the target policy defines the key; the rules end the local
# list in the order the source host held them. A rule whose path the target
# already maps as an equivalence is skipped with a FIXME in the build output,
# because deleting its key would delete that equivalence.
# /srv is a symlink to /var/srv on this base and the policy has no /var/srv alias;
# this makes every /srv rule, stock and custom, apply to the real path. The
# equivalence is added when absent and left alone when identical; a different
# target mapping stops the build with an instruction.
RUN eqs="$(semanage fcontext -l -C)" || { printf 'FIXME: could not list the target file contexts before adding the equivalence for %s; fix semanage in the base, or exclude this rule, then rebuild\n' '/var/srv' >&2; exit 1; }; \
    eq="$(printf '%s\n' "$eqs" | awk -v s='/var/srv' '$2 == "=" && $1 == s { print $3 }')"; \
    if [ -z "$eq" ]; then semanage fcontext -a -e '/srv' '/var/srv'; \
    elif [ "$eq" != '/srv' ]; then printf 'FIXME: %s is already equivalent to %s on the target, not %s; delete that equivalence with semanage fcontext -d -e %s %s, or exclude this rule, then rebuild\n' '/var/srv' "$eq" '/srv' "$eq" '/var/srv' >&2; exit 1; fi
RUN spec='/srv/www(/.*)?'; \
    eqs="$(semanage fcontext -l -C)" || { printf 'FIXME: could not list the target file contexts before replaying the rule for %s; fix semanage in the base, or exclude this rule, then rebuild\n' "$spec" >&2; exit 1; }; \
    if printf '%s\n' "$eqs" | awk '$2 == "=" { print $1 }' | grep -qxF -- "$spec"; then \
      printf 'FIXME: skipped the file context rule for %s; the target maps that path as an equivalence, which semanage fcontext -d would delete instead of a label; delete it with semanage fcontext -d -e <its target> %s, or exclude this rule, then rebuild\n' "$spec" "$spec" >&2; \
    else semanage fcontext -d "$spec" 2>/dev/null || true; \
      semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_content_t "$spec" \
      || semanage fcontext -m -t httpd_sys_content_t "$spec"; fi
# 1 custom SELinux port label(s) detected
RUN semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8081

# === Static Routes ===
# Static route file: etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/route-eth0
# Static route file: etc/iproute2/README

# === /etc/hosts Additions ===
# FIXME: These /etc/hosts entries need to be added to the image:
#   10.10.10.10 app.internal app
#   10.10.10.11 db.internal db

# === Proxy Configuration ===
# etc/profile.d/proxy.sh: export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.internal:3128
# etc/profile.d/proxy.sh: export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.internal:3128
# etc/profile.d/proxy.sh: export NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,.internal,github.com,githubusercontent.com,ghcr.io,quay.io,registry.redhat.io

# === /var directory provisioning ===
# /var directories with known ownership/mode provisioned via tmpfiles.d
COPY config/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/inspectah-var.conf /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/inspectah-var.conf
# FIXME: confirm the base image creates /var/lib/myapp; on the host myapp.service created it and no package owns that unit; if the base does not, uncomment the next line
#d /var/lib/myapp 0755 root root -

# === Validate bootc compatibility ===
RUN bootc container lint
